title: The Architectural Folio
critique: The architectural front has presence, but the old reverse split the venue and contact details into competing columns and left no natural place for a planner code. The email was too small relative to the headline.
improvement: The architectural front is preserved. A calmer reverse gives direct enquiries one clear column and the planner QR its own space.

title: The Venue Cipher
critique: The favourite reverse has an excellent expressive invitation, but its three lines compete with the contact column. Repeating all event categories in the lower left would crowd a new QR.
improvement: The expressive reverse is retained, with a wider contact column and a QR beneath the invitation. The complete facade remains a quiet venue signature.

title: The Private Invitation
critique: The admired ivory front is already coherent. Its former centred reverse has no suitable QR position without weakening its symmetry or making the contact details smaller.
improvement: The admired ivory front is unchanged. A navy reverse pairs a gold invitation with clear enquiries and a separate planner QR.

title: The Architectural Invitation
critique: The original counterchange is strong. The reverse repeated the front tagline and squeezed the email into a narrow blue column; adding a QR to that version would make the hierarchy worse.
improvement: The architectural front keeps its strong navy-and-ivory balance. A wider reverse contact panel improves reading, while the QR sits within the ivory invitation.

title: The Architectural Address
critique: The ceremonial centre was visually strong, but its heraldry no longer fits the venue brief. The sweeping reverse left too little space for a useful planner route.
improvement: The complete facade replaces the crest inside one broad pressed field. The staggered invitation survives, with enquiries aligned beside the planner QR.

title: The House Invitation
critique: The classical TH and expansive invitation are strong. The old reverse disperses the venue address and contact details into two small columns, while a planner QR needs protected space of its own.
improvement: The original TH silhouette and generous invitation are retained. Larger front captions and an ordered reverse make both the venue and the next step clearer.

title: The Glassford Address
critique: The memorable 85 and large venue name worked. The obsolete motto and crowded two-column reverse weakened the venue purpose and offered no route to planning.
improvement: The distinctive 85 and venue name are retained with improved alignment. The complete facade balances the invitation, above a clear contact and planner panel.

title: The Glassford Counterchange
critique: The selected counterchange composition is memorable, but its armorial shield, motto, Roman numerals and two impressed faces no longer serve the venue brief. The small right-hand email also needs a deliberate scale.
improvement: The original colour balance is retained, with the complete facade and Glassford Street address replacing heraldry. The reverse separates planning from direct enquiries.

title: House Cipher Invitation
critique: XIV and Union occupy the focal column while the contacts are undersized.
improvement: The classical TH mark is optically centred. An ivory reverse replaces the old inscription with an invitation, complete facade and a clear planner route.

title: Architectural Counterchange
critique: Crest and shield are the main subject and do not serve the new venue-only brief; repeating the badge on reverse weakens contact function.
improvement: The favourite navy-and-ivory composition is preserved. The complete gold facade replaces the shield, with an invitation and QR facing a clear contact panel.

title: House Cipher
critique: Front type must align optically with the monogram; reverse crest and huge stacked name compete with contacts.
improvement: The signature TH and navy reverse are retained. The complete facade replaces the crest, with clearer contact hierarchy and a discreet white QR square.

label: 01 v2
title: Oculus, Reconsidered
critique: The original portrait card invents coffered concentric stepped relief; it cannot be retained as tooling and lacks verified architectural fidelity.
improvement: Grand Hall photography gives the circular idea an authentic subject. One broad deboss replaces the stepped relief, and the landscape reverse adds a clear planner route.

title: Ivory Architectural Object
critique: Portrait format, crest, motto and armorial recess conflict with the current brief; original oxblood is outside the native palette.
improvement: The ivory front and leaflet-blue reverse are retained in landscape. A complete gold facade replaces heraldry, balanced by the venue name and planner QR.
